- MRI Findings:  Image Title: Pre-operative magnetic resonance Images (MRI)  Image Description: Showed fluid-filled sac (7 cm) and multinodal cyst without solid lesion. No contrast enhanced rim on the cyst. Contents showed high-intensity on T1-weighted image and relatively low-intensity on T1-weighted image consistent with hematoma.

records.query: Need the patient's serum tumor marker results (AFP, hCG, LDH) and histopathology/cytology report of the aspirated fluid or excised cyst wall, as the ultrasound showing a multilocular cyst attached to the testis does not exclude malignancy and these results are essential for confirming or ruling out scrotal/testicular malignancy.
records.text: - Pathological Examination:  - Gross examination showed two cysts (7.0 cm and 3.0 cm) attached to right testis  - Microscopic examination of smaller cyst showed single row of bland tall columnar cells  - Immunohistochemistry results: EpCAM(+), BerEP4(+), calretinin(−), D2-40(−), WT-1(+), estrogen receptor (ER)(+)(nearly 100%), progesterone receptor (PR)(+)(approximately 20%)  - No intracellular mucin, papillary growth or stromal invasion found.

bindings.label: Right scrotum is swollen and rapidly growing without local pain
A 50-year-old Japanese man, non-smoker, with hypertension treated with ARB daily and no known allergies
A puncture at a prior hospital yielded red-colored fluid
No history of trauma or infections including STDs; physical examination revealed swelling on the right side
Ultrasound and MRI show multilocular cystic lesion with septa, no solid component or enhancing rim, contents consistent with hematoma
Ultrasound shows multilocular cyst attached to testis with no testicular abnormalities
Pathology shows bland tall columnar cells lining the cyst with no stromal invasion or papillary growth
Immunohistochemistry: EpCAM+, BerEP4+, WT-1+, ER+, PR+, calretinin-, D2-40-
Red aspirate likely reflects prior hemorrhage within the cyst
Benign epithelial cyst of the testicular adnexa (e.g., mesothelial/epididymal cyst)
